title: Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps
summary: Given a pointer at index 0 in an array of size arrLen, at each step, you can move left, right, or stay in place within the array bounds.
statement: Given a pointer at index 0 in an array of size arrLen, at each step, you can move left, right, or stay in place within the array bounds. Calculate the number of ways to return to index 0 after exactly steps steps, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Start at index zero in an array of length arrLen.
Each step moves left, moves right, or stays, without leaving the array.
Return ways to be at index zero after exactly steps moves, modulo 1000000007.
hints: Only positions through steps/2 can participate in a path returning to zero.
Track counts at reachable positions and transition left, stay, and right each step.
Apply array bounds and the modulus.
The position after the final step partitions all paths; returning paths are exactly state zero.
editorial: The position after the final step partitions all paths; returning paths are exactly state zero.

tests.explanation: There are four valid three-step sequences returning to zero.
Stay-stay and right-left are the two returning sequences.
